mechanism_narrative: A higher current level of the federal funds rate directly increases the risk-free rate used in equity valuation models, leading to lower expected S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns show a positive correlation with FEDFUNDS (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.0% in the most recent monthly reading, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that suppresses corporate earnings growth and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3.0% over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts and retail sales indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline of HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases (i.e., the signal fails to predict negative returns in the majority of instances).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate profits, with the effect being most pronounced over a 60-day horizon.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts reading below 950.0 thousand units indicates a contraction in the residential construction sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 950.0 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher current level of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) signals elevated inflation, which erodes real corporate profits and increases the risk of monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns show a positive correlation with CPIAUCSL (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and quarterly GDP growth indicates a contraction in the real economy, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline of INDPRO and GDPC1 does not produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong retail sales (RSAFS > 400,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns as consumer spending supports corporate revenue growth, with the effect being most pronounced over a 20-day horizon.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS > 400,000 over any 3-year rolling window.
